title: Scaling psychedelic-assisted therapy for depression and PTSD
bottleneck: MDMA-assisted therapy showed Phase 3 efficacy for PTSD and psilocybin shows promise for depression, but delivery requires 6-8 hours of two trained therapists per session, strict set-and-setting protocols, and Schedule I regulatory status. The model that proved efficacy in trials is economically and logistically unscalable.
why_it_blocks: If the most promising new psychiatric treatments in decades cannot be delivered beyond boutique clinics, their population impact will be negligible regardless of efficacy.
current_state: MDMA-assisted therapy faced FDA setbacks over trial-conduct concerns; Australia allows limited prescribing. Research into shorter-acting analogs and group formats aims to cut delivery costs, but regulatory pathways remain uncertain. Group therapy formats and shorter-acting compounds like 5-MeO-DMT could cut per-patient therapist hours dramatically, but efficacy data for these scaled models are preliminary.
